newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Electricidad waiting on 13 pct rate rise.
newsitem.headline: Electricidad waiting on 13 pct rate rise.

text.p: Leading Venezuelan electricity company Electricidad de Caracas is waiting on the final passage of an expected 13 percent rate rise, company officials said.

"The rise has already been approved by the Council of Ministers, it's just waiting on final approval from the Ministry of Energy and Mines," said the high-placed source who asked not to be identified.
The Ministry of Energy and Mines carries the decisive voice in approving electricity rate rises.
"The rise will help our second half results, but it's not enough to meet our increase in costs," the official said. "Our dividend will have to remain suspended for the meantime."
The source added that plans for the eventual issue of an American Depositary Receipts (ADR) were also on ice.
"We're absolutely ready to go, but with the rates still not fully sorted out, now is not the moment."

Electricidad received rate increases in August and May this year of 9.65 and 28 percent. When company executives complained the hikes did not compensate for inflation or exchange rate losses, Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta said further rate adjustments might come depending on the outcome of company audits.
The source added the government was considering implementing next January a new system for adjusting electricity rates: "That's what we hear, but we don't yet know any details."
